items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: And then by studying the Glenn Miller scores, like Bill Finegan’s scores and stuff like that, I learned a lot.

ctx.x: You mentioned your stint with Glenn Miller and you made your arranging mistakes then. What were the arranging mistakes that you learned about and didn’t do later?

Writing too much. Just writing everything. You know I’ll back up and say that the first symphony I heard was at Geneseo State Teacher’s College. My father and mother took us to see an orchestra, the Rochester Symphony. And I’d never heard anything like that in my life. And I hadn’t heard a real full big band at that point either, right? You know that was the first large ensemble live that I heard. You know in high school we had concert bands and all that. But anyway, when they took a break I looked at the stage…

Yes. If you look at a score and everybody’s playing all the time, you have trouble. But I know in the past I’ve had instances where I look at a score I’ve written and, especially if it’s for a large group, and, “Gee I haven’t written anything for the bassoon in 20 measures, I’d better give him something to do.” And that is not really the way to think I guess.
